algorithm.title: Abdominal Pain of Less than 48 Hours Duration: Diagnosis.

cell.label: Presume ectopic pregnancy TV US + quantitative β-HCG.
Presume diverticulitis: CT of abdomen and pelvis with IV/oral contrast.
Presume urolithiasis: CT of abdomen and pelvis without contrast.
Presume appendicitis: If equivocal, CT of abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast.
Presume intestinal obstruction: CT of abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast.
Presume AAA: imaging if diagnosis in question or preop if patient stable, OR if unstable.
Pain out of proportion to examination?
Presume mesenteric ischemia: CT angiogram, lactic acid level, or abdominal angiogram (see Diagnostic Tests table).
Presume pancreatitis: obtain lipase and amylase levels If positive, then US of abdomen.

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: TV US, transvaginal ultrasound; US, ultrasound; AAA, abdominal aortic aneuerysm; UTI, urinary tract infection; U/A, urinalysis; HCG, human chorionic gonadotropin; LLQ, left lower quadrant; RUQ, right upper quadrant; RLQ, right lower quadrant; PID, pelvic inflammatory disease.

algorithm.title: Abdominal Pain of More than 48 Hours Duration: Diagnosis.

cell.label: Presume IBS. Screen for alarm features.*
Presume GERD. Screen for alarm features.*
Presume dyspepsia. Screen for alarm features.* Consider H. pylori stool Ag.

See . Consider less serious diagnoses (gastroenteritis, dysmenorrhea, simple pregnancy, diarrhea, constipation, muscular strain). Consider less common diagnoses (IBD, cancer). Use the clinical decision rule to determine the likelihood that serious disease is present.

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: IBS, Irritable bowel syndrome; GERD, gastroesophageal reflux disease; H. pylori stool Ag., Helicobacter pylori stool antigen; IBD, Irritable bowel disease; GI, gastrointestinal

Alarm features: Bleeding (melena, hematochezia, hematemesis), early satiety, progressive dysphagia, odynophagia, persistent vomiting, chronic severe diarrhea, recurring fever, previous GI malignancy, previous documented peptic ulcer, family history of GI cancer, unexplained weight loss greater than 10% body weight or greater than 10 lb, lymphadenopathy, abdominal mass, anemia.
